c1.evidence: Offer: Serve as a Precinct Election Official (PEO) for Linn County, IA on Election Day.

c2.evidence: Requirements: Live in and be registered to vote in Linn County, Iowa; be able to work from 6 a.m. until close of polls; attend the required training classes.

c3.evidence: Payout: $225 for election day. Precinct election officials are also paid a flat rate for online training and hourly for attending in-person training prior to the election; mileage is reimbursed.

c4.evidence: Time required: Work from 6 a.m. until close of polls (polls open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.); close the polling place at 8 p.m. and complete closing requirements. Roughly 14-16 hours on Election Day plus training.

s1.note: Pay is a fixed per-election-day rate set by the county: precinct election officials are paid $225 for election day.

s2.note: Election workers must be able to work from 6 a.m. until close of polls; polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.; workers close the polling place at 8 p.m. and complete closing requirements.

s3.note: Training is required; PEOs are paid a flat rate for online training and hourly for attending in-person training before the election, plus mileage to and from training and the polling place.

s4.note: Linn County elections are county-run through the county auditor's Election Services office; payment for working an election is made 2-5 weeks after the election.

s5.note: PEO duties include setting up the polling place and voting equipment the morning of Election Day, guiding voters through the process, closing the polling place at 8 p.m., and completing closing requirements.

s6.note: Eligibility: must live in and be registered to vote in Linn County, Iowa; cannot be a current candidate or closely related to any opposed candidate on the ballot; precinct teams are balanced between registered Democrats and Republicans.

s7.note: No guaranteed extra payout beyond the posted schedule; the $225 election-day rate is fixed per election, with additional flat/hourly training pay.
